TRANSCATHETER AORTIC VALVE REPLACEMENT PROCEDURE NOTE

Indication: Severe symptomatic native aortic stenosis in a patient at intermediate surgical
risk per heart team consensus.

Procedure: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) was performed via right common
femoral arterial access under conscious sedation. Following pre-dilation balloon
valvuloplasty of the native calcified valve, the delivery system was advanced across the
native aortic valve under fluoroscopic and transesophageal echocardiographic guidance.

Device: Edwards SAPIEN 3
Size: Ultra 26mm

The valve was deployed under rapid ventricular pacing in good position with no significant
paravalvular leak on final aortography and echocardiography. Post-deployment hemodynamics
showed a mean gradient of 7 mmHg across the transcatheter valve with an effective orifice
area of 1.9 cm2. Access site hemostasis was achieved with a vascular closure device.

Disposition: The patient was transferred to the recovery unit in stable condition for
continued post-procedure monitoring.
